intake.line: Retained: Prava slides a laminated org chart across a laminate desk and tells Milo, warmly, that he has been retained and is a strong culture fit for Reconciliations. Milo, who has never been told his boredom was valuable, says yes before anyone offers him a choice, and Prava writes his name somewhere he cannot see.

partition.line: Sometimes It's Quieter: In the windowless Marrow District, Milo is given a lanyard, a desk and a trainer, Zara Okafor, who teaches him tenure, quotas and the one graduation per quarter in short flat sentences and never looks up. He mistakes her courtesy for friendship; she, without saying so, starts measuring him.

bell.line: The File of Halvard Bell: Milo opens the account of Halvard Bell, a dentist who spent ninety years in Retention and was restructured at nine that morning. For the first time a closure has a face and a career attached, and Milo, reading it more carefully than the quota requires, finds he is slower than usual.

summons.line: Filed Through Reconciliations: Zara and Milo submit the restructuring of Edric Thane's own pooled account through the department built to close accounts, every box correct, every appendix cited. Within the hour Milo receives a calendar invitation to his quarterly review in the corner office, and Zara, for the first time, looks up.

corner office.line: Mr. Voss: Edric Thane receives Milo courteously, reviews his numbers, and offers him exactly what he once wanted: recognition, promotion, the path Edric himself climbed. Milo, recognising himself across the desk six centuries on, understands that saying yes would make him the next Edric, and declines.

discrepancy.line: It Doesn't Reconcile: Halvard's ninety years of tenure do not add up to the balance Milo is meant to zero; the difference has already left, flowing upward into a single pooled account at the top of the org chart. Milo turns to tell Zara as if he has found a bug; she does not look up, says 'Again,' and makes him run the numbers until he understands it is not a bug, ending the act with the discrepancy his and no longer deniable.
